findings.title: Validate returned identifier types before comparing the injected selection
findings.observation: actual_ids is compared directly with expected_ids. A str subclass containing 'dotnet' can override __eq__ to return True for 'repository'; the exact-ID guard accepts it and the adapter analyze callback executes.
findings.impact: The new returned-identity consistency check does not enforce its advertised exact fixed IDs and invokes collaborator-defined equality before rejecting malformed identifiers. This is a trusted-DI contract failure, not a claim that request JSON can select arbitrary code or that publication grants are bypassed.
findings.correction: After reading each identifier once, reject non-exact str values and out-of-range fixed-ID lengths before equality. Retain exact ordered tuple comparison against normalized expected_ids and fail with the existing ValueError before any analyze callback.
findings.focused_regression: Count equality and analysis with a wrong-text str subclass/non-string sentinel; require zero custom equality calls and zero analyze calls on rejection. Cover oversized plain identifier without changing valid one-read/one-analysis behavior.
